title: Wirecard: A €24bn Star and the €1.9bn Nobody Could Find
summary:
Wirecard collapse explained from the audit, regulator and court records.

In June 2020 Germany's payments star admitted that €1.9 billion, about a quarter of its balance sheet, probably did not exist. Using Wirecard's own announcements, KPMG's special investigation, BaFin's orders, the Bundestag inquiry, the auditor watchdog's sanctions and reporting from the Munich trial, we explain how the 'third-party acquiring' business worked, why the regulator filed a complaint naming journalists, who has been held to account and where the trial stands. Markus Braun denies all charges and is presumed innocent; no verdict has been reached.

scenes.say: In June 2020, a German tech company admitted that one point nine billion euros on its balance sheet probably did not exist.

visual.label: cash in trust accounts that could not be verified
visual.src: Wirecard ad hoc, 18 Jun 2020; Al Jazeera, 22 Jun 2020

scenes.src: Wirecard ad hoc, 18 Jun 2020; Al Jazeera, 22 Jun 2020

scenes.say: That was about a quarter of everything the company said it owned.
Less than two years earlier, Wirecard had been worth more than twenty-four billion euros, and had taken Commerzbank's place in Germany's top share index.

visual.text: Wirecard joins the DAX, replacing Commerzbank

scenes.say: Its former chief executive, Markus Braun, has now been on trial in Munich for almost four years. He denies every charge, and no verdict has been reached.

This is the story told through the paperwork: the audit, the regulator and the special investigation. And one document, published two months before the collapse, already said the key question could not be answered.

visual.title: KPMG report
lines: Main reason given: partners did not fully cooperate
visual.src: KPMG special investigation report, 27 Apr 2020, pp. 12–13

scenes.src: KPMG special investigation report, 27 Apr 2020, pp. 12–13

scenes.say: Wirecard processed card payments for online shops. Its share price passed one hundred and ninety euros in September 2018.
At that peak, investors valued it at more than twenty-four billion euros.

visual.label: market value at the September 2018 peak

scenes.say: Reuters reported that it was worth more than Deutsche Bank when it joined the index.

visual.label: Wirecard's value when it joined the DAX: more than €23bn

scenes.say: To the outside world, it looked like Germany's answer to Silicon Valley. But a large part of its profit came from business that other companies did on its behalf.

visual.text: Wirecard presented fraudulent balance sheets over several years.

scenes.say: To understand what went missing, you need to understand three words: third-party acquiring.

visual.src: KPMG special investigation report, 27 Apr 2020, p. 14

scenes.src: KPMG special investigation report, 27 Apr 2020, p. 14

scenes.say: According to KPMG, Wirecard referred customers to three partner companies, which processed their card payments.

visual.title: Third-party acquiring, as KPMG described it
items: Wirecard refers merchants to a partner
The partner processes the card payments
Wirecard books the fees as its own revenue
The partner's commission is booked as a cost

scenes.say: Wirecard booked the fees as its own revenue. In return, it promised to cover the partners' losses, and that promise was secured with cash held by a trustee.

visual.title: How the escrow worked
lines: Wirecard indemnifies the partner against losses
!Secured by cash in trustee escrow accounts
Escrow balances broadly tracked partner revenue

scenes.say: KPMG found that the companies running this business produced the predominant share of the group's operating profit.

visual.label: of group operating profit (EBIT) came from the partner-business companies
visual.sub: KPMG: depends on how costs are allocated

scenes.say: So the profit depended on partners outside Wirecard, and the cash supposedly sat with a trustee outside Wirecard. Anyone checking had to rely on other people's paperwork.

visual.title: Who held what
items: Cash: held by an outside trustee

scenes.say: The first public warnings came in January 2019, when the Financial Times published allegations of accounting irregularities in Wirecard's Asian business.
Police in Singapore raided Wirecard's offices there in February.

visual.text: Singapore police raid Wirecard's local offices

scenes.say: Germany's financial regulator, BaFin, then did something unusual. On the eighteenth of February 2019, it banned new bets against Wirecard's shares.

visual.title: General Administrative Act
lines: !Ban on new net short positions, with immediate effect

scenes.say: And in April, BaFin filed a criminal complaint with Munich prosecutors over suspected market manipulation. AP later reported that the people it named included two Financial Times journalists.

visual.text: BaFin complaint names two FT journalists among others

scenes.say: That investigation was dropped in September 2020. Prosecutors said the reporting had been, quote, fundamentally accurate.

visual.by: Munich prosecutors, as reported by AP, Sep 2020

scenes.say: By then, Wirecard no longer existed as a going concern.

visual.label: from BaFin's complaint to Wirecard's insolvency

scenes.say: Under pressure, Wirecard hired KPMG for a special investigation. The report was dated the twenty-seventh of April 2020.
For the years 2016 to 2018, KPMG could neither confirm nor rule out that the partner business existed as reported. It used a German word: Untersuchungshemmnis. An obstacle to the investigation.

visual.text: Insoweit liegt ein Untersuchungshemmnis vor. (In this respect, there is an obstacle to the investigation.)

scenes.say: The reason, KPMG wrote, was the partners' lack of willingness to cooperate fully and transparently.

visual.title: Why it could not be verified
lines: Partners did not cooperate fully and transparently
Dec 2019 data: no indications of deviations so far

scenes.say: It also reported that about one billion euros of payments into trust accounts could not be verified.

visual.label: trust-account deposits KPMG could not verify

scenes.say: KPMG was told that the original trustee in Singapore had ended the relationship at the end of 2019 and stopped responding. A new trustee took over, with accounts at banks in the Philippines.

visual.text: Singapore trustee exits; accounts move to Philippine banks

scenes.say: Wirecard's own announcement of the report led with a different line: no incriminating evidence of balance-sheet manipulation had been identified.

visual.title: Same report, two readings
items: Wirecard, 28 Apr: no incriminating evidence identified
KPMG, p. 12: existence of partner revenue could not be verified
visual.src: Wirecard ad hoc, 28 Apr 2020; KPMG report, p. 12

scenes.src: Wirecard ad hoc, 28 Apr 2020; KPMG report, p. 12

scenes.say: Wirecard's auditor was EY. Its 2019 accounts were due on the eighteenth of June 2020.
That morning, Wirecard announced that EY could not obtain sufficient audit evidence for one point nine billion euros held in trust accounts.

visual.title: Wirecard AG
lines: About a quarter of the balance sheet

scenes.say: The company said there were indications that spurious balance confirmations had been given to the auditor. If audited accounts were not ready by the next day, lenders could terminate loans of about two billion euros.
The next day, Markus Braun resigned. In Manila, two Philippine banks, BPI and BDO, said the documents showing Wirecard deposits were false, and that Wirecard was not their client.

visual.title: What the Philippine banks said
items: BPI: documents were false; not a client
BDO: documents were false; not a client
Central bank: money did not appear to have entered the country

scenes.say: On the twenty-second of June, Wirecard said there was a, quote, prevailing likelihood that the one point nine billion euros did not exist.

visual.text: There is a prevailing likelihood that the bank trust account balances in the amount of 1.9 billion EUR do not exist.

scenes.say: Braun was arrested that day, and released on five million euros' bail.
On the twenty-fifth, Wirecard filed for insolvency. Reuters reported it was the first member of the DAX to go out of business.
Fifteen banks had lent it one point seven five billion euros. Bond investors had lent five hundred million more. One lender told Reuters: the money is gone.
The shares had lost ninety-eight per cent since the auditor's refusal a week earlier.

visual.label: share price fall in the week after EY's refusal
visual.src: CNN, 25 Jun 2020; Reuters via Malay Mail, 25 Jun 2020

scenes.src: CNN, 25 Jun 2020; Reuters via Malay Mail, 25 Jun 2020

scenes.say: In July 2020, Munich prosecutors had Braun arrested again, along with two other former executives.

The charges included commercial gang fraud and market manipulation. Prosecutors alleged that, as early as 2015, the suspects decided to inflate the balance sheet. They said a key witness and documents had helped their investigation.

visual.title: The allegation
lines: !Alleged plan from 2015 to inflate the balance sheet

scenes.say: The indictment ran to four hundred and seventy-four pages. The trial opened on the eighth of December 2022, with three defendants.

Prosecutors put the damage at about three billion euros. Braun denies everything. His defence says the business was real, and that others, led by the former board member Jan Marsalek, stole the profits.

visual.label: damage alleged by prosecutors
visual.sub: Braun denies all charges and is presumed innocent

scenes.say: According to the news agency dpa, the presiding judge has called that argument speculative.

visual.title: The judge on the defence
lines: Defence: the business was real; others took the profits

scenes.say: The former Wirecard manager in Dubai, Oliver Bellenhaus, has confirmed the prosecution's account on essential points. The former chief accountant denies the charges.

visual.title: The three defendants
items: Markus Braun, ex-CEO: denies all charges
Oliver Bellenhaus, ex-Dubai manager: confirmed the prosecution's account
Former chief accountant: denies the charges

scenes.say: dpa now puts the booked bank balances that cannot be found at one point seven billion euros. The insolvency administrator, Michael Jaffé, has still found no sign that the money ever existed.

visual.label: booked bank balances that cannot be found
visual.sub: Administrator: no sign the money ever existed

scenes.say: Marsalek himself vanished in 2020. In a London spy trial that ended in 2025, the convicted ring was described as directed by Marsalek, an alleged Russian agent wanted by Interpol. He has not faced trial.

visual.title: Jan Marsalek
lines: Wanted by Interpol after Wirecard's collapse
!Described as directing the convicted spy ring
Alleged Russian agent; has not faced trial
visual.src: PA via Express & Star, 7 Mar 2025; LTO, 9 Nov 2022

scenes.src: PA via Express & Star, 7 Mar 2025; LTO, 9 Nov 2022

scenes.say: dpa reports that the court plans to set a final two-week deadline for the defence's evidence motions on the eleventh of November. Dates for closing speeches and a verdict have not been set.

visual.text: Court plans to set final deadline for evidence motions

scenes.say: So who has been held to account so far?
In April 2023, Germany's audit watchdog, APAS, found that EY had breached its professional duties in auditing Wirecard's accounts for 2016 to 2018. The decisions could still be challenged.

EY was fined five hundred thousand euros, and banned for two years from taking on new statutory audits of public-interest companies. Five individual auditors were fined between twenty-three thousand and three hundred thousand euros.

In September 2024, a Munich civil court ordered Braun and two other former board members to pay one hundred and forty million euros plus interest, for an unsecured loan and a bond purchase made without proper checks.

visual.label: civil damages, Munich Regional Court I
visual.sub: Judgment of 5 Sep 2024, case 5 HK O 17452/21

scenes.say: BaFin's president left in early 2021. The finance ministry said the scandal had shown that German financial supervision needed reorganising.

visual.text: The Wirecard scandal has revealed that Germany's financial supervision needs a reorganization.

scenes.say: And a parliamentary inquiry questioned one hundred and five witnesses. Its report ran to more than two thousand pages. Three opposition parties called it a collective failure of supervision.
Here is what we take from the paperwork. This part is our analysis.
Lesson one. A confirmation is only as good as the chain that produced it. EY was given balance confirmations that, by Wirecard's own account, were probably spurious.

visual.title: Lesson 1
items: Cash confirmed by a trustee is not cash seen at a bank

scenes.say: Lesson two. When most of the profit depends on partners who won't open their books, that is the finding. KPMG said so in writing two months before the collapse.
Lesson three. In our view, a regulator that treats critics as the problem loses time it cannot get back. Here, the journalists' reporting was later called fundamentally accurate.

visual.label: from the first FT allegations to the insolvency

scenes.say: If this sounds familiar, our Patisserie Valerie case file is another company whose accounts hid what was really in the bank. It's on screen now.

visual.sub: Another set of accounts that didn't match the bank

scenes.say: The Munich verdict could come within months. Subscribe if you want the follow-up when the court rules. Our next case file is Greensill Capital.
